operator_io_quirks: All table/column names are plain ASCII, no spaces or mixed case; quoting still required for safety but no BIRD-style hazards.
Tiny DB (max 15 rows); read_schema sampling is trivial, no huge-table path exercised.

DATETIME columns store text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (space separator, no T, no fractional seconds); ts_fuzzer dispatch is 'Date|Number(int elements)' because first element does not parse as int -> Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.
Courses.course_id is VARCHAR(100) but Student_Course_Registrations.course_id is INTEGER and FK-references it; declared-type mismatch across the FK edge (parent text '301', child integer 301).

Student_Course_Attendance has a COMPOSITE FK (student_id, course_id) -> Student_Course_Registrations(student_id, course_id); pragma foreign_key_list yields two single-column rows, so read_schema sees two separate FKs, not one composite.
Students.student_id, Candidates.candidate_id are PKs that are ALSO FKs to People.person_id (PK-as-FK); same for People_Addresses.person_id/address_id (non-PK FK to PK).
Student_Course_Registrations.student_id FK -> Students.student_id, which is itself an FK to People.person_id: FK chain depth 2 (People -> Students -> Registrations -> Attendance).
Courses.other_details is 100% NULL (distinct=0, storage=['null']); String sampler with empty elements -> p:=1, always fresh random strings.
Addresses.country has distinct=1 ('USA'); String sampler will mostly emit random charset strings, not 'USA'.
Addresses.zip_postcode CHAR(20) stores short numeric strings ('862','716'); String fuzzer will treat as int-like and add +-1 variants.
People.password stores 40-char hex; String fuzzer length range [40,41] from elements, so fresh strings are 40-41 chars over a-zA-Z0-9() space.
No views, triggers, or unique indexes beyond PKs; no CHECK constraints; no dangling FKs (all parent_exists=true).
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on DATETIME columns: template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S, range from min/max of 5 sampled originals (e.g. 2008-2018), so fresh dates cluster in that window; implausible for 'future' or 'before 2008' predicates -> likely FN.

Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs (person_id, address_id, course_id-as-int): range [-10^4,10^4] with +-1/+-2 perturbation; original IDs are small (111,121,...) so fresh IDs are wildly out of range -> joins on ID equality mostly miss -> FN on ID-predicate queries.

String fuzzer on names/cities/emails: random charset a-zA-Z0-9() space, length from element range; 'USA' country, 'Pass'/'Fail' outcome, 'A'/'B'/'C'/'D' qualification will be replaced by random strings -> FN on equality predicates like qualification='A'.

Courses.course_id VARCHAR but child FK INTEGER: TS draws child values from parent's generated text values (e.g. '301'), inserts into INTEGER column -> sqlite affinity converts to 301; joins still work but type-strict comparisons may differ.

Composite PK (student_id, course_id) on Registrations/Attendance: sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate tuples; with small sizes (1-30) and Number fuzzer over [-10^4,10^4], collisions rare -> few drops, but FK draws from parent's filtered column may produce tuples not in parent -> FK violations silently skipped at insert (foreign_keys OFF).

PK-as-FK (Students.student_id -> People.person_id): child draws from parent's final person_id values, so student_id subset of person_id; if People is small (1-30) and Students larger, many Students rows fail PK uniqueness or FK -> row loss.
People_Addresses.date_from/date_to both Date fuzzer independently -> date_from > date_to frequently; queries asserting date_from < date_to will see implausible rows -> FN.
Courses.other_details all-NULL: String sampler with no elements -> p=1, always fresh random strings; queries 'WHERE other_details IS NULL' will find none -> FN.
Small table sizes (choose_table_sizes: 1-30 or 30-230) mean joins often empty; TS misses ties/duplicates because PK/unique filtering removes them -> FP on DISTINCT-vs-not and COUNT queries.
No CHECK constraints, so TS never exercises constraint-violation paths; NOT NULL violations (e.g. registration_date) are the main insert-failure source.
